question: Should the experimental Claws lifecycle own a new core, persisted-state `claws update` planning contract now, or should this stack pause until the RFC and ownership boundaries receive explicit maintainer sponsorship?
rationale: The patch is not a repair to an established behavior: it creates a durable core CLI/schema surface and defines consent semantics across sandbox, tools, plugins, MCP, schedules, and ownership state. Review cannot safely choose that product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core planner
options.body: Keep this as the read-only core primitive, require current-head real behavior proof, and land it only with its prerequisite lifecycle slices in the intended order.

options.title: Pause for RFC direction
options.body: Defer the PR stack until maintainers confirm that grouped Claw lifecycle management belongs in core rather than another product surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core planner
recommendation.body: Keep this as the read-only core primitive, require current-head real behavior proof, and land it only with its prerequisite lifecycle slices in the intended order.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is assigned and has already reviewed the planner’s core lifecycle invariants.
